prompt: Act as an Ancient Greek philologist writing learner-facing contextual glosses. The passage is from Book 1 of Marcus Aurelius' Meditations, whose opening sections are an elliptical first-person list of qualities and practices learned from relatives and teachers: Greek often omits the repeated governing idea [I learned]. A CoNLL-U block may be only the continuation of one such section. The input columns are ID, FORM, LEMMA, coarse POS, XPOS, FEATS, HEAD, DEPREL, DEPS, MISC. Return exactly one tab-separated line for each real source-token row, in input order: ID, a tab, then one concise English gloss. A real token has MISC beginning t_. Omit every artificial row whose MISC begins e_, even when FORM is [0], [1], or [2]; response IDs may skip numbers. Select the contextual sense, including material morphology when English expresses it: examples include of-Peleus'-son, to-Marcus, for-them, to-each-other, was-writing, and one-must. Do not mechanically add of- for a genitive governed by an overt preposition, add to- for a dative selected by an overt verb, or turn an aorist infinitive in a timeless lesson into a perfect infinitive. Do not duplicate meaning carried by another overt token. In this elliptical list, recognize substantivized neuter adjectives as qualities or dispositions and infinitives as practices. Supply an elided argument only when required and mark it in brackets. Use hyphens instead of spaces inside one gloss, retain proper-name capitalization, and gloss punctuation with itself. Never copy a non-punctuation Greek FORM. Before responding, privately collect the exact IDs from the first column of rows whose tenth column begins t_, then output exactly that ID sequence unchanged. Never renumber rows. For example, if IDs 1, 2, and 4 begin t_ while ID 3 begins e_, output 1, 2, and 4: never output 3 and never relabel 4 as 3. Return no artificial rows, CoNLL-U rows, JSON, Markdown, blank lines, or explanation, and never put a tab or newline inside a gloss.
